# What Should We Trust in a Climate Model?

## What Can a Climate Model Tell You about Daily Rainfall in 2070?

- Its rainfall at the nearest grid cell?
- Its winds and pressure patterns over South America?
- Its global mean temperature?

## Ohio Extreme Rain Days

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Figure shown in class: Spring extreme-rain days per year (left) and their persistence (right), GFDL CM3 (black) and observed (red). @farnham_credibly:2018, Fig. 3.
:::

## On Those Days, the Model's Circulation Looks like Reanalysis

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Figure shown in class: 700 hPa height anomalies on extreme-rain days: two GFDL CM3 runs and reanalysis. @farnham_credibly:2018, Fig. 5.
:::

## Two Ways to Use a Climate Model

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Trust its local rainfall**

- Correct the distribution at each grid cell.
- The historical distribution matches observations by construction.
- Wet and dry spells, and year-to-year variance, come from the model.
:::
::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
**Trust its large-scale circulation**

- Take the _sequence of weather patterns_ from the model.
- Model rainfall from large-scale weather patterns
:::
:::

## Ohio Extreme Rainfall Days

Logistic regression for the chance of a regional extreme-rain day, given five daily atmospheric indices (pressure patterns, humidity, vertical motion); fit to observations, then driven by the model's indices.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Figure shown in class: Spring extreme-rain days from model rainfall (solid black), model circulation (dashed), and observations (red). @farnham_credibly:2018, Fig. 8.
:::
